## Objective

Phase 4 of `planning/gfw_analysis_plan.qmd`: estimate how the **gradient of
fishing effort with distance from the leases** changed between the stages
(Before–After–Gradient, Methratta 2020, 2021), and how effort responded to
each foundation's installation, its 500 m safety zone and active
construction.

| Step | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | Descriptive BAG: rate by distance band × stage (season-standardised) and × stage × season, with cell-bootstrap intervals |
| 2 | Event time: monthly rate by band around each project's first foundation, season-adjusted, with bootstrap intervals |
| 3 | Simulation power: the minimum detectable BAG effect (MDE) per dataset × gear |
| 4 | Pre-trend equivalence test (TOST), with margins from step 3 |
| 5 | Stage × season BAG per dataset × gear |
| 6 | Timing BAG with the Ørsted covariates (foundation distance, construction, safety zones) |
| 7 | Formal mobile vs fixed contrast |
| 8 | Rate ratios with MDEs, predicted densities, diagnostics, leave-one-vessel-out, fleet-size sensitivity |

**Interim models (decision 2026-10-20, D-047).** Phase 5 chooses the final
spatial structure and families. Until then every model here uses the form
Phase 5 recommends: `sdmTMB` with an SPDE spatial field (mesh cutoff
`r params$mesh_cutoff_km` km), NB2 for vessel presence (VP) and Tweedie for
apparent fishing effort (AFE, with delta-Gamma alongside for the stage ×
season models). Everything is cached with `fit_cached()`, so Phase 5 can
refit with its choices by changing the specification only.

**Domains** (caveat 13). Each dataset × gear is modelled on the cells it
used in Stage 1 (`domain`), so cells that were never fished before
construction (structural zeros) do not dilute the contrast, and the domain
cannot depend on the outcome. Pole-and-line AFE is not modelled (plan,
"Scope per gear"); it appears in the descriptive steps only.

**Reading the results.** Every BAG effect is a rate ratio: the change in a
band's rate since Stage 1, **relative to the 8–15 km ring**. It measures
**redistribution** within the study area, not a net change in regional
effort (plan, "Limits of the within-AOI BAG"). Each estimate is reported
next to its gear's MDE, so a null reads "no effect larger than the MDE".

## Libraries and shared code

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(sf)
  library(sdmTMB)
  library(DHARMa)
})

source("r/paths.R")
source("r/gfw_helpers.R")
source("r/analysis_helpers.R")
source("r/bag_helpers.R")

doc_params <- if (isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) params else {
  hdr <- knitr::knit_params(readLines(file.path(root, "r/09_bag.qmd"), warn = FALSE))
  lapply(hdr, function(p) p$value)
}
# every Phase 0 table, vessel record, model specification and support
# decision, the same as 09a fitted (D-101); sets qparams and paths.
# get_fit() and the leave-one-vessel-out reader only read the cache
source("r/bag_specs.R", local = knitr::knit_global())

# straight after the seed, before the specifications existed (D-101)
set.seed(42)

fig_dir <- file.path(paths$bag, "figures")
tab_dir <- file.path(paths$bag, "tables")
for (d in c(fig_dir, tab_dir)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

outputs <- character()
save_tab <- function(df, name) {
  f <- file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  write_csv(df, f, na = "")
  outputs <<- c(outputs, f)
  invisible(f)
}
save_fig <- function(p, name, width = 10, height = 6) {
  f <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".png"))
  ggsave(f, p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
  outputs <<- c(outputs, f)

kable_round <- function(df, digits = 3) {
  df |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, digits))) |> knitr::kable()
}
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))

if (length(missing_fits) > 0)
  stop(length(missing_fits), " of ", length(all_specs), " main fits are not cached for this pipeline ",
       "(first: ", missing_fits[[1]]$id, "). Render r/09a_bag_fit.qmd first", call. = FALSE)
```


## Read the Phase 0 tables

`r/bag_specs.R` reads the analysis tables 05 writes (cell × stage, × stage ×
season, × month and × season-year, per dataset and gear) and the
active-construction shares at the sensitivity radii (02a). The modelled
dataset × gear combinations (plan, "Scope per gear"):

```{r}
ss_models |> knitr::kable()
```


## Step 1: descriptive BAG

The rate by distance band in each stage (season-standardised, caveat 8: the
mean of the 12 month-of-year rates, so stages with different calendar mixes
compare fairly), and in each stage × season. Intervals resample cells within
each band (`r qparams$n_boot` draws). All cells, all three gears.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
# plotting order; near (inside + 0–2) and mid (2–8 km) are the merged
# scheme's bands (D-076)
band_order <- c("inside", "0-2", "near", "2-4", "4-8", "mid", "8-15")
desc_stage <- map_dfr(set_names(datasets), function(ds) {
  st[[ds]] |>
    transmute(gear_class, stage, dist_band, hours = rate_std, expo = area_km2) |>
    group_by(gear_class, stage) |>
    group_modify(\(g, k) boot_band_rate(g, B = qparams$n_boot)) |> ungroup()
}, .id = "dataset") |>
  mutate(dist_band = factor(dist_band, band_order))
desc_ss <- map_dfr(set_names(datasets), function(ds) {
  ss[[ds]] |>
    transmute(gear_class, stage, season, dist_band, hours, expo = months * area_km2) |>
    group_by(gear_class, stage, season) |>
    group_modify(\(g, k) boot_band_rate(g, B = qparams$n_boot)) |> ungroup()
}, .id = "dataset") |>
  mutate(dist_band = factor(dist_band, band_order))
save_tab(desc_stage, "bag_descriptive_stage")
save_tab(desc_ss, "bag_descriptive_stage_season")

gradient_plot <- function(d, title) {
  ggplot(d, aes(dist_band, rate, colour = stage, group = stage)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = 0.25, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = stage_cols) +
    labs(x = "distance band (km from the nearest lease; inside = within a lease)",
         y = "hours per km² per month", colour = NULL, title = title)
}
p <- gradient_plot(desc_stage, "Effort gradient by stage (season-standardised; 95% cell-bootstrap intervals)") +
  facet_grid(dataset ~ gear_class, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(dataset = ds_label))
save_fig(p, "bag_descriptive_stage", height = 7)
p

for (ds in datasets) {
  p <- gradient_plot(filter(desc_ss, dataset == ds),
                     paste(ds_label[[ds]], "effort gradient by stage, within each season")) +
    facet_grid(season ~ gear_class, scales = "free_y")
  save_fig(p, sprintf("bag_descriptive_stage_season_%s", ds), height = 7)
  print(p)
}
```

The descriptive BAG ratio: each band's rate divided by the 8–15 km ring's,
by stage. Its change from Stage 1 is what the models estimate.

```{r}
desc_ratio <- desc_stage |>
  group_by(dataset, gear_class, stage) |>
  mutate(ratio_to_ring = rate / rate[dist_band == "8-15"]) |> ungroup() |>
  select(dataset, gear_class, stage, dist_band, ratio_to_ring) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = ratio_to_ring)
save_tab(desc_ratio, "bag_descriptive_ratio_to_ring")
desc_ratio |> filter(dist_band %in% c("inside", "0-2")) |> kable_round(2)
```

## Step 2: event time

Monthly density per cell around each project's first foundation
(`months_since_first_found`, −`r qparams$event_window` to
+`r qparams$event_window`), by distance band and nearest project. Season is
removed by dividing each value by its dataset × gear × band's month-of-year
index (that month's mean over the whole series, relative to the overall
mean). Intervals resample cells (199 draws, enough for a plotted band).

```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
event <- map_dfr(set_names(datasets), function(ds) {
  m <- month[[ds]]
  idx <- m |> group_by(gear_class, dist_band, moy) |> summarise(mm = mean(density), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(gear_class, dist_band) |> mutate(season_index = mm / mean(mm)) |> ungroup()
  m |>
    filter(between(months_since_first_found, -qparams$event_window, qparams$event_window)) |>
    left_join(select(idx, gear_class, dist_band, moy, season_index), by = c("gear_class", "dist_band", "moy")) |>
    mutate(adj = if_else(season_index > 0, density / season_index, 0)) |>
    group_by(gear_class, nearest_project, dist_band) |>
    group_modify(function(g, k) {
      cells <- unique(g$cell_id)
      by_cell <- split(g, g$cell_id)
      set.seed(42)
      reps <- map_dfr(seq_len(199), function(b) {
        bind_rows(by_cell[sample(cells, replace = TRUE)]) |>
          group_by(months_since_first_found) |> summarise(v = mean(adj), .groups = "drop")
      })
      g |> group_by(months_since_first_found) |> summarise(rate = mean(adj), .groups = "drop") |>
        left_join(reps |> group_by(months_since_first_found) |>
                    summarise(lo = quantile(v, 0.025), hi = quantile(v, 0.975), .groups = "drop"),
                  by = "months_since_first_found")
    }) |> ungroup()
}, .id = "dataset") |>
  mutate(dist_band = factor(dist_band, band_order))
save_tab(event, "bag_event_time")

for (ds in datasets) {
  p <- event |> filter(dataset == ds, dist_band %in% c("inside", "0-2", "8-15")) |>
    ggplot(aes(months_since_first_found, rate, colour = dist_band, fill = dist_band)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(inside = "#d03b3b", `0-2` = "#eb6834", `8-15` = "#52514e"),
                        aesthetics = c("colour", "fill")) +
    facet_grid(gear_class ~ nearest_project, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "months since the nearest project's first foundation",
         y = "season-adjusted density (h km⁻² month⁻¹)", colour = "band (km)", fill = "band (km)",
         title = paste(ds_label[[ds]], "event time around each project's first foundation"))
  save_fig(p, sprintf("bag_event_time_%s", ds), height = 9)
  print(p)
}
```

## Vessel records

Primary records per vessel, read once. They serve the term-support check
below (how many vessels back each term, D-076) and the leave-one-vessel-out
refits (step 8). `vessel_month` holds each vessel's hours per cell and
month; the support check matches it to the model rows by cell and stage ×
season, or by cell and time-step end for the timing models.
They are read in `r/bag_specs.R` (`vessel_month`, `vessel_hours`,
`vessel_ss`, `vessel_step`).


## Model specifications

Every model is written once as a **specification**: its data, formula and
settings (the cache key for `fit_cached()`) and a self-contained fit
function. The specifications live in `r/bag_specs.R`, shared with
`09a_bag_fit.qmd`, which fits them, and `09b_bag_power.qmd` (D-101). This
report only reads the cache: a fit that is missing stops it, naming the
notebook to render.

**Convergence.** A fit is accepted when the Hessian is positive definite,
the optimiser converged and the gradients are small (`sanity()`).
`se_magnitude_ok` is not required: when the depth effect is close to linear,
the depth smooth's wiggliness parameter goes to zero and its standard error
is uninformative. That is harmless, and it is the common case for the sparse
gears.


### Term support (D-076)

Before any fit, every 0/1 fixed-effect column of every model is counted:
the rows it switches on, the **positive** rows among them (hours > 0), and
the distinct cells and vessels with effort in those rows
(`term_support()`). A term is supported if it has at least
`r qparams$support_min_positive` positive rows from at least
`r qparams$support_min_cells` cells and `r qparams$support_min_vessels`
vessels. The thresholds are parameters, set before fitting. The rule is
applied the same way to every model, with no case-by-case choices:

- **BAG terms** (stage × band; construction and development × band):
  if any lacks support, the model pools its bands (near = inside + 0–2 km,
  mid = 2–8 km). If the pooled terms still lack support, the model is not
  fitted and that gear is reported descriptively.
- **Lead terms** (leads model): if any lacks support, the three lead bins
  pool into one (24–1 months). If that still fails, no leads model is
  fitted.
- **Foundation distance** (*h*(·)): bands coarsen from 0–2 / 2–5 / 5–10 km
  to 0–5 / 5–10, then 0–10, and the term is dropped if even that fails.
- **Other indicators** (post-construction × band, active construction):
  dropped one by one if unsupported.

The decisions are logged in `bag_support_rules`, and every count in
`bag_term_support`. No new term enters a main model after this point.
New questions go into separate sensitivity fits, as the leads model does
(D-076).


```{r}
# the stage × season models the support rule kept, and their size
ss_sets |> transmute(id, bands, cells = map_int(data, \(d) n_distinct(d$cell_id)), rows = map_int(data, nrow),
                     positive_rows = map_int(data, \(d) sum(d$hours > 0))) |> knitr::kable()

# the timing and pre-trend models' rows by period
timing_sets |> filter(!map_lgl(pre_data, is.null)) |>
  transmute(id, step, pre_bands, timing_bands = bands, rows = map_int(pre_data, nrow),
            cells = map_int(pre_data, \(d) n_distinct(d$cell_id)),
            pre_rows = map_int(pre_data, \(d) sum(d$phase == "pre")),
            stage1_rows = map_int(pre_data, \(d) sum(d$pre_bin %in% "baseline")),
            pre_2016_2019_rows = map_int(pre_data, \(d) sum(d$phase == "pre" & d$step_end <= as.Date("2019-12-31"))),
            dev_early_rows = map_int(pre_data, \(d) sum(d$pre_bin %in% "dev_early")),
            lead_24_13_rows = map_int(pre_data, \(d) sum(d$pre_bin %in% "lead_24_13")),
            lead_12_1_rows = map_int(pre_data, \(d) sum(d$pre_bin %in% "lead_12_1"))) |> knitr::kable()

# the support rule's decisions and every count behind them (D-076)
save_tab(support_rules, "bag_support_rules")
support_rules |> knitr::kable()
save_tab(term_support_tab, "bag_term_support")

# the fleet values each model sees (raw counts, before the log and centring)
fleet_vp |> imap_dfr(\(f, step) f |> group_by(gear_class) |>
  summarise(steps = n(), min = min(fleet), median = median(fleet), max = max(fleet), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(time_step = step, .before = 1)) |> knitr::kable()
```


## Model fits

Every specification is fitted by `09a_bag_fit.qmd` (D-101), in parallel,
with at most a few large fits at once (D-097) and each fit's progress
logged (D-099). Its fit log, read here: fit time, convergence, optimiser
iterations, whether the fit was warm-started from its parent, and the
mesh size (D-098).

```{r}
fit_log_path <- file.path(tab_dir, "bag_fit_log.csv")
input_files <- c(input_files, fit_log_path)
read_csv(fit_log_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |> knitr::kable()
```


## Step 3: simulation power

**Run by `09b_bag_power.qmd`, only after Phase 5 settles the base model
(D-096, D-101).** Power simulates from the base model, so until then this
report runs without it: every MDE is unknown (NA), estimates are read
without an equivalence margin, the pre-trend test uses the plan's
placeholder margin, and no gear is marked descriptive-only for want of an
MDE. Once 09b has run, its results are read here, but only while the base
models and power settings they came from are still the current ones.


For each dataset × gear: fit the **base model** (the stage × season model
without the BAG terms), simulate `r qparams$power_nsim` new datasets from it
with **new spatial random fields** each time (`simulate(re_form = ~0)`), so
spatial uncertainty is included (conservative). Inject a known BAG effect
in Stage 3, in the shape the pre-registration fixes for each gear (plan,
@sec-bag-power; D-091), by binomial thinning for VP counts and scaling for
AFE (`power_effect_factor()`, `r/bag_helpers.R`). Effects are planted by
each cell's own band, whatever band scheme the refit uses:

- **Matching scenario**, which defines the MDE, at *e* ∈
  {`r paste(100 * unlist(qparams$power_effects), collapse = ", ")`}%: the
  mean times (1 − *e*) in the `inside` band alone for a gear fitted with
  the four bands, so the MDE is that of its Stage 3 × inside headline; in
  `inside` and `0–2` km for a gear whose bands are pooled (D-076), the
  cells of its Stage 3 × near headline.
- **Fading gradient**, for the gradient test's power only, at
  *e* = `r 100 * qparams$power_fade_effect`%: (1 − *e*) inside,
  (1 − *e*/2) at 0–2 km and (1 − *e*/4) at 2–4 km, a displacement that
  weakens with distance. Its *e* = 0 run is the matching scenario's, since
  nothing is planted.

The full BAG model is refitted to each. Two things are scored: the
headline rate ratio (power: 95% CI excludes 1; bias; coverage), and the
gradient test, the Wald test of all Stage 3 × band terms at α = 0.05
(power, and at *e* = 0 its false-positive rate). The same simulated datasets
are reused across effect sizes and scenarios, so the curves differ only by
the effect.

**Second pass (D-094).** After the `r qparams$power_nsim`-simulation pass,
the smallest effect with power ≥ 0.8 in the matching scenario, and the size
below it when that is above 0, get more simulations, up to
`r qparams$power_nsim_bracket`, from a second draw (`seed = 43`). The MDE is
the smallest tested effect with power ≥ 0.8, scored on all of a size's
simulations. A gear that reaches 0.8 nowhere gets no second pass.

**Timing models (D-094).** A monthly timing refit takes hours, so each
timing model's power is simulated on a **season-year proxy**: the timing
model rebuilt at season-year by the support rule (D-076), its base model
without the construction × band terms, and (1 − *e*) planted in each cell's
construction-phase seasons in the headline's bands (inside, or inside and
0–2 km when pooled), at *e* ∈
{`r paste(100 * unlist(qparams$timing_power_effects), collapse = ", ")`}%.
The construction × inside (or near) term is scored. Fixed AFE's timing
model is at season-year already, so its result is its actual power.

**Radius recovery (D-065, D-094).** For VP mobile at season-year only:
*λ* planted as (1 − *e*)<sup>*a*</sup> on the 5 km active-construction share
*a* (true *λ* = log(1 − *e*)), at *e* ∈
{`r paste(100 * unlist(qparams$radius_effects), collapse = ", ")`}%, and each
simulation refitted with the share at
`r paste(unlist(qparams$radius_km), collapse = ", ")` km. Scored: *λ*'s power
at 5 km; recovery (5 km has the lowest AIC); at *e* = 0, how often another
radius beats 5 km by more than 2 AIC units; and *λ*'s bias at 5 km and at
the radius with the lowest AIC (the winner's curse). A radius may be chosen
from the data only if recovery ≥ 0.8 at an *e* where *λ*'s power ≥ 0.8.

The simulations, refits, power curves and figures are in
`09b_bag_power.qmd`; the tables later steps need are read here.

```{r power-results}
# Step 3's results from 09b, used only if their fingerprint (the base
# models' cache hashes and the power settings) matches the current one
pr <- if (file.exists(power_results_path)) readRDS(power_results_path)
power_current <- !is.null(pr) && identical(pr$fingerprint, power_fingerprint())
if (power_current) {
  input_files <- c(input_files, power_results_path)
  mde <- pr$mde; gradient_power <- pr$gradient_power; timing_mde <- pr$timing_mde
  radius_choice_allowed <- pr$radius_choice_allowed
  message("Step 3 power read from 09b (written ", pr$written, ")")
} else {
  # Step 3 not run, or run on other models or settings (D-096): the tables
  # later steps read, with every power result unknown. descriptive_only is
  # NA, not TRUE, so bag_gate() does not fail a gear for an MDE that was
  # never estimated; bag_verdict() with an NA MDE gives only "decrease" /
  # "increase" / "inconclusive"; the pre-trend margin falls back to the
  # plan's placeholder (pretrend_margin())
  mde <- ss_sets |> transmute(id, dataset, gear, bands, mde = NA_real_, fpr = NA_real_, descriptive_only = NA)
  gradient_power <- tibble(id = character(), scenario = character(), effect = numeric(), power = numeric())
  timing_mde <- tpower_sets |>
    transmute(id, bands, mde = NA_real_, mde_basis = "power not run (D-096)")
  # the D-065 rule needs the recovery runs, so the radius stays at 5 km
  radius_choice_allowed <- FALSE
  message(if (is.null(pr)) "Step 3 power not run (D-096)" else
    "Step 3 results are from other base models or settings; not used", ": every MDE is NA")
}
mde |> kable_round(2)
timing_mde |> kable_round(2)
radius_choice_allowed
```


## Step 4: pre-trend equivalence test

Each cell's pre-construction months (`phase == "pre"`) at the timing model's
step (monthly; season-year for fixed AFE), with a band-specific linear
trend *θ*<sub>b</sub> relative to the 8–15 km ring. A band is equivalent if
its 90% CI lies inside ±*δ*, with *δ* from the gear's MDE extrapolated over
the gap between the Stage 1 and Stage 3 midpoints (`pretrend_margin()`).
The spatial field here is persistent only (no time-varying field), since
the trend terms are the subject.

**Two diagnostic windows (D-075).** Stage 2 (October 2020 to the first
works) holds site surveys, boulder clearance and, at its start, COVID, so a
departure in the full pre-period may be early disturbance rather than a
long-run trend. The same test therefore runs on **Stage 1 only** (January
2016 – September 2020) and on **2016–2019** (time steps ending by December
2019, without COVID), with the same margin *δ*. The full pre-period verdict
remains the gate; the two diagnostics only say where a departure comes from
(`pretrend_reading()`). They are shorter, so "inconclusive" is more likely.

```{r}
mid <- \(s) dev_stages$start[dev_stages$stage == s] + (dev_stages$end[dev_stages$stage == s] - dev_stages$start[dev_stages$stage == s]) / 2
dt_years <- as.numeric(mid("Stage 3") - mid("Stage 1")) / 365.25
dt_years

# band trends and their TOST outcomes from one pre-trend fit
pretrend_tab <- function(sp, delta) {
  tidy(get_fit(sp)) |> filter(str_detect(term, "^dist_band.*:year_c$")) |>
    mutate(band = str_remove_all(term, "dist_band|:year_c")) |>
    rowwise() |> mutate(tost_band(estimate, std.error, delta)) |> ungroup() |>
    select(band, est, se, lo90, hi90, lo95, hi95, delta, outcome)
}
pretrend_windows <- c(full = "full pre-period", stage1 = "Stage 1 only", pre_covid = "2016–2019")
# every gear with a stage × season model; its pre-trend uses that model's
# band scheme (D-076)
pretrend_all <- timing_sets |> filter(!map_lgl(spec_pre, is.null)) |>
  mutate(res = pmap(list(id, spec_pre, spec_pre_s1, spec_pre_1619), function(id, s0, s1, s2) {
    m <- mde$mde[mde$id == id]
    delta <- pretrend_margin(if (length(m)) m else NA_real_, dt_years)
    bind_rows(full = pretrend_tab(s0, delta), stage1 = pretrend_tab(s1, delta),
              pre_covid = pretrend_tab(s2, delta), .id = "window")
  })) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, res) |> unnest(res)
save_tab(pretrend_all, "bag_pretrend_windows")

# the gate: the full pre-period, as before
pretrend <- pretrend_all |> filter(window == "full") |> select(-window)
save_tab(pretrend, "bag_pretrend")
pretrend_gate <- pretrend |> group_by(id, dataset, gear) |>
  summarise(verdict = pretrend_verdict(outcome), delta = first(delta), .groups = "drop")
save_tab(pretrend_gate, "bag_pretrend_verdict")
pretrend_gate |> kable_round(4)

# where a departure comes from: the gate's verdict next to the diagnostics
pretrend_where <- pretrend_all |> group_by(id, dataset, gear, window) |>
  summarise(verdict = pretrend_verdict(outcome), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = window, values_from = verdict) |>
  mutate(reading = pretrend_reading(full, stage1, pre_covid))
save_tab(pretrend_where, "bag_pretrend_reading")
pretrend_where |> knitr::kable()

# one row per band and window, offset vertically so the three windows sit
# side by side; the margin is shaded as before
win_cols <- c("full pre-period" = "black", "Stage 1 only" = "#2a78d6", "2016–2019" = "#eb6834")
band_lv <- c("inside", "0-2", "near", "2-4", "4-8", "mid")
pt_plot <- pretrend_all |>
  mutate(window = factor(pretrend_windows[window], pretrend_windows),
         y = match(band, band_lv) + c(0.2, 0, -0.2)[as.integer(window)])
p <- ggplot(pt_plot, aes(est, y, colour = window)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = -delta, xmax = delta, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), fill = "grey92", inherit.aes = FALSE,
            data = distinct(pt_plot, id, dataset, gear, delta)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo95, xmax = hi95), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo90, xmax = hi90), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(band_lv), labels = band_lv, trans = "reverse") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = win_cols, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ id, ncol = 3, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "band trend relative to the 8–15 km ring (log scale per year)", y = NULL,
       title = "Pre-construction trends by window: 90% (thick) and 95% (thin) CIs; grey = equivalence margin ±δ") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
save_fig(p, "bag_pretrend", height = 6)
p
```

## Random-field check (D-077)

**Read this before Step 5.** The fixed-effect terms are capped by the
support rule (D-076); the random fields are checked here instead, by how
well each structure **predicts data it has not seen**. Only predictive
scores are shown: no BAG effect is read from these fits, so the choice of
field cannot be steered by the answer it gives.

- **Stage × season models: spatial-block cross-validation.** The study area
  is cut into square blocks at least *ρ*<sub>0</sub> wide (Phase 3's
  practical range for the dataset × gear, `global_rho0.csv`, rounded up),
  and whole blocks are dealt to `r qparams$cv_folds` folds
  (`spatial_block_folds()`). Each fold is held out in turn, the model is
  fitted to the rest, and the held-out rows are scored by their log
  likelihood. Three structures, same fixed effects and family:
  - **shared**: one spatial field for all stages (`spatiotemporal = "off"`);
  - **iid per stage** (the fitted model): the shared field plus an
    independent field per stage;
  - **AR1 per stage**: the shared field plus stage fields correlated from
    one stage to the next.

  Higher summed held-out log likelihood is better. The rule is fixed in
  advance (plan, "Term support and model complexity"): another structure
  replaces the fitted one only if it scores higher in total, scores higher
  in at least four of the five folds (`folds_better`), and has no failed
  fold (`folds_ok` below `folds`: a non-positive-definite Hessian).
- **Timing models: AIC.** Five-fold CV of the monthly timing models would
  take days (each fit is 3–6 h), so the AR1 year field is compared with the
  persistent field alone by AIC on the full data. Both fits are by maximum
  likelihood with the same fixed effects. A variance at its boundary makes
  AIC conservative about dropping the field, which is the safe direction
  here. The AR1 field is dropped only if that lowers AIC by more than 2
  (`d_aic` above 2).

The fitted models are **not** changed by this section in an interim
render. Under the plan, a structure that meets the rule replaces the
fitted one in Phase 5's refit, logged as a new decision; the BAG terms stay
as frozen.

```{r field-check, eval = isTRUE(get0("qparams")$field_check)}
# cross-validation scores; Δ against the fitted model (iid per stage)
cv_scores <- cv_sets |>
  mutate(cv = map(spec, get_fit)) |>
  transmute(id, structure, block_km, rho0_censored, blocks,
            folds_ok = map_int(cv, \(r) sum(r$pdHess)), folds = map_int(cv, \(r) length(r$pdHess)),
            sum_loglik = map_dbl(cv, "sum_loglik"), fold_loglik = map(cv, "fold_loglik")) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(ref = fold_loglik[structure == "iid per stage"],
         d_loglik = sum_loglik - sum_loglik[structure == "iid per stage"],
         # folds where this structure scores higher than the fitted one
         folds_better = map2_int(fold_loglik, ref, \(a, b) sum(a > b))) |>
  ungroup() |> select(-ref)
cv_tab <- cv_scores |> mutate(fold_loglik = map_chr(fold_loglik, \(v) paste(round(v, 1), collapse = "; ")))
save_tab(cv_tab, "bag_field_cv")
cv_tab |> select(id, structure, block_km, blocks, folds_ok, folds, sum_loglik, d_loglik, folds_better) |>
  kable_round(1)

# timing models: AIC with and without the AR1 year field
field_aic <- field_timing |>
  transmute(id, ar1 = map(spec_timing, get_fit), off = map(spec_nofield, get_fit)) |>
  transmute(id, converged_ar1 = map_lgl(ar1, fit_ok), converged_off = map_lgl(off, fit_ok),
            aic_ar1 = map_dbl(ar1, AIC), aic_off = map_dbl(off, AIC),
            d_aic = aic_ar1 - aic_off)   # negative: the AR1 year field earns its place
save_tab(field_aic, "bag_field_aic")
field_aic |> kable_round(1)
```


## Step 5: stage × season BAG

The Stage 2 × band terms (`stageStage 2:dist_bandinside`, `…0-2`) compare
Stage 2 with Stage 1 before any foundation or cable went in, so they are
this model's **anticipation estimate** (D-075): a Stage 2 effect means
fishers responded to site surveys, boulder clearance or the prospect of
construction, and Stage 3's terms then measure change from a Stage 1
baseline that Stage 2 had already moved away from.

```{r}
ss_fits <- ss_sets |>
  mutate(fit = map(spec, get_fit),
         fit_dg = map(spec_dg, \(s) if (is.null(s)) NULL else get_fit(s)))
ss_fits |> transmute(id, converged = map_lgl(fit, fit_ok),
                     converged_delta_gamma = map_lgl(fit_dg, \(f) if (is.null(f)) NA else fit_ok(f))) |>
  knitr::kable()

# each model's own BAG terms, from its band scheme (D-076)
bag_rr <- ss_fits |>
  mutate(rr = map2(fit, terms, \(f, tm) rate_ratios(tidy(f), tm))) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, bands, rr) |> unnest(rr) |>
  mutate(stage = str_extract(term, "Stage [23]"), band = str_extract(term, "inside|0-2|near")) |>
  left_join(select(mde, id, mde, descriptive_only), by = "id")
save_tab(bag_rr, "bag_rate_ratios")
bag_rr |> select(id, bands, stage, band, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p, mde, descriptive_only) |> kable_round(3)
```

The delta-Gamma parts for AFE: whether a cell is fished (binomial) and how
much given fished (Gamma). Opposite signs would mean the hurdle is needed on
substance (Phase 5).

```{r}
dg_rr <- ss_fits |> filter(dataset == "afe") |>
  mutate(rr = map2(fit_dg, terms, \(f, tm) bind_rows(
    rate_ratios(tidy(f, model = 1), tm) |> mutate(part = "occupancy (odds ratio)"),
    rate_ratios(tidy(f, model = 2), tm) |> mutate(part = "intensity given fished")))) |>
  select(id, rr) |> unnest(rr)
save_tab(dg_rr, "bag_delta_gamma_parts")
dg_rr |> select(id, part, term, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p) |> kable_round(3)
```

### Full stage × band grid and gradient test (D-091)

The headline is one term, Stage 3 × inside (or near), but BAG is about the
gradient, so the pre-registration (plan, @sec-bag-prereg) also fixes two
things that describe its whole shape:

- **The full grid.** Every stage × band term of each headline model:
  Stages 2 and 3 × the four bands (inside, 0–2, 2–4, 4–8 km), or × near and
  mid where the bands are pooled (D-076), each against the 8–15 km ring and
  relative to Stage 1. These are estimates, not verdicts: the robustness
  checks are not applied to them. They show whether a change is confined to
  the leases, spreads into 0–2 km, or fades with distance.
- **The gradient test.** A Wald test that all Stage 3 × band terms are zero
  at once (`wald_joint()`, `r/bag_helpers.R`): χ² with one degree of freedom
  per band, from the fit's fixed-effect covariance, at α = 0.05. It answers
  whether the gradient changed shape anywhere, with one test, not one per
  band. It sits beside the headline verdict and never alters it, and a
  non-rejection reads *no evidence of a gradient change*, not "no change"
  (`gradient_verdict()`). For AFE it is also computed on the delta-Gamma
  fit, over the Stage 3 × band terms of both parts together (the parts'
  estimates are correlated, so the joint covariance is used).

```{r}
# the full grid: every stage × band term of each model's band scheme
bag_grid <- ss_fits |>
  mutate(rr = map2(fit, bands, \(f, b) rate_ratios(tidy(f), grid_terms_of(b)))) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, bands, family, rr) |> unnest(rr) |>
  mutate(stage = str_extract(term, "Stage [23]"), band = str_remove(term, ".*dist_band"))
save_tab(bag_grid, "bag_rate_ratio_grid")
bag_grid |> select(id, bands, stage, band, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p) |> kable_round(3)

# The Wald test of a model's Stage 3 × band terms (D-091), by fit_wald()
# (r/bag_helpers.R), which labels the fixed effects and their covariance from
# the fit's own design matrix: sdmTMB's vcov() leaves them unlabelled when
# the formula has a smooth, as every BAG model does. `delta = TRUE` tests
# both parts of a delta-Gamma fit together, with their cross-part
# covariance. Terms that cannot be matched give NA, never a test on
# mispaired estimates and variances.
stage3_wald <- function(fit, bands, delta = FALSE) {
  fit_wald(fit, grid_terms_of(bands, stages = 3), parts = if (delta) c(1, 2) else 1)
}

# one row per fit: the headline fit (NB2 for VP, Tweedie for AFE in these
# interim models) and, for AFE, the delta-Gamma fit. A fit that did not
# converge has no readable covariance, so its test is NA rather than read
gradient_test <- bind_rows(
  ss_fits |> transmute(id, dataset, gear, bands, model = family, headline_fit = TRUE,
                       converged = map_lgl(fit, fit_ok), w = map2(fit, bands, stage3_wald)),
  ss_fits |> filter(!map_lgl(fit_dg, is.null)) |>
    transmute(id, dataset, gear, bands, model = "delta_gamma (both parts)", headline_fit = FALSE,
              converged = map_lgl(fit_dg, fit_ok),
              w = map2(fit_dg, bands, \(f, b) stage3_wald(f, b, delta = TRUE)))) |>
  unnest(w) |>
  mutate(across(c(chi2, p), \(x) if_else(converged, x, NA_real_)),
         gradient = gradient_verdict(p)) |>
  arrange(id, desc(headline_fit))
save_tab(gradient_test, "bag_gradient_test")
gradient_test |> select(id, bands, model, converged, chi2, df, p, gradient) |> kable_round(4)
```

The gradient profile: one panel per dataset × gear, the rate ratio of each
band against the 8–15 km ring, relative to Stage 1, with one line per
stage. The dashed line at 1 is no change since Stage 1; a gradient that
changed shape bends away from it, and how it bends says where the change
is.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
profile <- bag_grid |>
  mutate(band = factor(band, intersect(band_order, unique(band)))) |>
  # the panel names the band scheme, since a pooled profile has two points
  # per stage, not four (D-076), and the gradient test's reading
  left_join(gradient_test |> filter(headline_fit) |> transmute(id, gradient, p_grad = p), by = "id") |>
  mutate(panel = paste0(id, " (", bands, "): ", coalesce(gradient, "gradient test not available"),
                        if_else(is.na(p_grad), "", sprintf(", p = %.3f", p_grad))))
p <- ggplot(profile, aes(band, rr, colour = stage, group = stage)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = rr_lo, ymax = rr_hi), size = 0.25, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = stage_cols) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(55)) +
  labs(x = "distance band (against the 8–15 km ring)", y = "rate ratio since Stage 1 (log scale)",
       colour = NULL, title = "BAG gradient profile: every stage × band term (D-091)",
       subtitle = "95% CIs; panel titles give the Wald test of all Stage 3 × band terms")
save_fig(p, "bag_gradient_profile", height = 9)
p
```

Caveat 17: from installation, a foundation's 500 m zone covers most of its

```{r}
length(zone_cells)
bag_rr_nozone <- ss_sets |>
  mutate(rr = map2(spec_nozone, terms, \(s, tm) rate_ratios(tidy(get_fit(s)), tm))) |>
  select(id, rr) |> unnest(rr)
save_tab(bag_rr_nozone, "bag_rate_ratios_no_zone_cells")
bag_rr_nozone |> select(id, term, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi) |> kable_round(3)
```

### Predicted densities by band × stage

Population-level predictions (no random fields), at the domain's mean
terrain, in hours per km² per month, per season.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 7
pred_grid <- function(fit, d) {
  nd <- expand_grid(stage = factor(bag_stage_levels, bag_stage_levels),
                    # the model's own band levels: full or merged (D-076)
                    dist_band = factor(levels(d$dist_band), levels(d$dist_band)),
                    season = factor(c("AprSep", "OctMar"), c("AprSep", "OctMar"))) |>
    mutate(depth_m = mean(d$depth_m), slope_z = 0, bpi_z = 0, x_km = mean(d$x_km), y_km = mean(d$y_km),
           stage_num = as.integer(stage))
  p <- predict(fit, newdata = nd, re_form = NA, se_fit = TRUE, offset = rep(0, nrow(nd)))
  nd |> mutate(rate = exp(p$est), lo = exp(p$est - 1.96 * p$est_se), hi = exp(p$est + 1.96 * p$est_se))
}
pred <- ss_fits |> mutate(p = map2(fit, data, pred_grid)) |> select(id, dataset, gear, p) |> unnest(p) |>
  mutate(dist_band = factor(dist_band, band_order))
save_tab(pred, "bag_predicted_density")
p <- ggplot(pred, aes(dist_band, rate, colour = stage, group = stage)) +
  geom_line() + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = stage_cols) +
  facet_grid(id ~ season, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "distance band", y = "predicted hours per km² per month", colour = NULL,
       title = "Model-predicted gradient by stage (interim stage × season BAG)")
save_fig(p, "bag_predicted_density", height = 9)
p
```

### Residual diagnostics (DHARMa)

```{r}
diag <- ss_fits |>
  mutate(res = map(fit, function(f) {
    set.seed(42)
    r <- dharma_residuals(simulate(f, nsim = 250, type = "mle-mvn"), f, return_DHARMa = TRUE, plot = FALSE)
    cell_r <- recalculateResiduals(r, group = f$data$cell_id)
    xy <- f$data |> distinct(cell_id, x_km, y_km)
    xy <- xy[match(unique(f$data$cell_id), xy$cell_id), ]
    tibble(uniformity_p = testUniformity(r, plot = FALSE)$p.value,
           dispersion_p = testDispersion(r, plot = FALSE)$p.value,
           zero_inflation_p = testZeroInflation(r, plot = FALSE)$p.value,
           spatial_autocorr_p = testSpatialAutocorrelation(cell_r, x = xy$x_km, y = xy$y_km, plot = FALSE)$p.value)
  })) |>
  select(id, res) |> unnest(res)
save_tab(diag, "bag_dharma")
diag |> kable_round(4)
```

## Step 6: timing BAG

Stages are replaced by each cell's own exposure, from the Ørsted dates
(`02a`):

- `phase`: the nearest project's pre / construction / post-construction,
  coded as a construction indicator plus construction × band terms (the BAG
  terms of this model), and post-construction × band terms. Only SFW reaches
  post-construction, and every SFW-nearest cell is inside a lease or within
  2 km, so the post terms exist for those two bands only and are relative to
  the area-wide trend, not to the outer ring;
- `development` (D-075): pre-construction months from Stage 2 on (October
  2020 to the nearest project's first works), with development × band
  terms `dx_*`. So "pre" in the construction terms is Stage 1 only, and the
  `dx_*` terms estimate any anticipation (site surveys, boulder clearance)
  instead of folding it into the baseline;
- `found_band`: distance to the nearest installed foundation, 0–2, 2–5 and
  5–10 km, against "none within 10 km" (the plan's *h*(·), as bands);
- `active_construction`: a foundation going in that month within 5 km (*λ*);
- `sz_share`: share of the cell inside an active USCG safety zone (*κ*),
  so the foundation terms measure the response beyond the mandated
  exclusion;
- a cyclic month-of-year smooth and a year smooth (AIS uptake and regional
  trend; season and season-year trend for fixed AFE).

The spatial field is persistent plus an AR1 field over years (plan, Phase
6 sketch).

Only the timing models that pass the term-support rule are fitted (D-076).
A gear without one is listed in `bag_support_rules` with the reason, and
its construction-phase response is read from the stage × season BAG or from
VP. The band scheme, foundation-distance cut and dropped terms of each
fitted model are listed there too.

```{r}
# every reported term under either band scheme and any foundation-distance
# cut; each model reports the ones it has (D-076)
found_lv <- c("0-2", "2-5", "5-10", "0-5", "0-10")
timing_terms <- c("cx_inside", "cx_0_2", "cx_near", "post_inside", "post_0_2", "post_near",
                  band_cols("dx", "full"), band_cols("dx", "merged"), paste0("found_band", found_lv), "active", "sz_share")
# only the models the support rule kept
timing_fits <- timing_sets |> filter(!map_lgl(spec_timing, is.null)) |> mutate(fit = map(spec_timing, get_fit))
timing_fits |> transmute(id, step, converged = map_lgl(fit, fit_ok)) |> knitr::kable()

timing_rr <- timing_fits |>
  mutate(rr = map(fit, function(f) {
    t <- tidy(f)
    rate_ratios(t, intersect(timing_terms, t$term))
  })) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, step, rr) |> unnest(rr) |>
  # each model's construction × inside (or near) MDE from Step 3 (D-094),
  # with its basis: a monthly model's is its season-year proxy's, whose band
  # scheme (`mde_bands`) may differ from the monthly model's
  left_join(select(timing_mde, id, timing_mde = mde, mde_basis, mde_bands = bands), by = "id")
save_tab(timing_rr, "bag_timing_rate_ratios")
timing_rr |> select(id, term, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p, timing_mde, mde_basis) |> kable_round(3)

p <- timing_rr |> filter(str_detect(term, "found_band")) |>
  mutate(dist = factor(str_remove(term, "found_band"), found_lv)) |>
  ggplot(aes(dist, rr, colour = gear)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = rr_lo, ymax = rr_hi), position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = gear_cols) + scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, labeller = labeller(dataset = ds_label)) +
  labs(x = "distance to the nearest installed foundation (km)",
       y = "rate ratio vs none within 10 km (log scale)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Turbine-distance response h(·), beyond the safety zones and active construction")
save_fig(p, "bag_timing_found_distance", height = 4.5)
p
```

### Anticipation: event-time leads (D-075)

The timing model refitted with development split by months to the cell's
first construction step: more than 24 months before (`dev_early`), 24–13
(`lead_24_13`) and 12–1 (`lead_12_1`), each with band terms, against Stage 1.
A band term near 1 in every bin means no anticipation; a fall that deepens
toward the works means fishers moved off before construction began, and
shows when. For fixed AFE (season-year steps) the bins are whole
half-years. The construction and foundation terms are reported for the main
timing model above; here only the lead terms are read.

```{r}
# l241: the pooled 24–1 month bin, used when the three bins lack support (D-076)
lead_bins <- c(de = "more than 24 months before", l24 = "24–13 months before", l12 = "12–1 months before",
               l241 = "24–1 months before")
lead_cols <- unlist(map(names(lead_bins), \(p) c(band_cols(p, "full"), band_cols(p, "merged"))))
# only the models the support rule kept
lead_rr <- timing_sets |> filter(!map_lgl(spec_timing_leads, is.null)) |>
  mutate(fit = map(spec_timing_leads, get_fit),
         converged = map_lgl(fit, fit_ok),
         rr = map(fit, function(f) {
           t <- tidy(f)
           rate_ratios(t, intersect(lead_cols, t$term))
         })) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, step, bands, converged, rr) |> unnest(rr) |>
  mutate(bin = factor(lead_bins[str_extract(term, "^[a-z0-9]+")], lead_bins),
         band = factor(str_replace(str_remove(term, "^[a-z0-9]+_"), "_", "-"),
                       c("inside", "0-2", "near", "2-4", "4-8", "mid")))
save_tab(lead_rr, "bag_timing_leads")
lead_rr |> select(id, converged, bin, band, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p) |> kable_round(3)

p <- ggplot(lead_rr, aes(bin, rr, colour = band, group = band)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = rr_lo, ymax = rr_hi), position = position_dodge(0.5), size = 0.25) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(0.5), linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ id, ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "time before the nearest project's first works", y = "rate ratio vs the 8–15 km ring, against Stage 1 (log scale)",
       colour = "band", title = "Anticipation: band effects in the months before construction") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
save_fig(p, "bag_timing_leads", height = 5)
p
```

## Step 7: mobile vs fixed

A joint stage × season model per dataset, each gear on its own domain, with
a `gear × stage × band` interaction. The three-way terms test whether fixed
gear's BAG effect differs from mobile gear's.

```{r}
# the three-way terms of each dataset's band scheme (gc_bands, D-076)
gear_contrast <- imap_dfr(gc_specs, function(s, ds) {
  fit <- get_fit(s)
  rate_ratios(tidy(fit), paste0("gearFIXED:", bag_terms_of(gc_bands[[ds]]))) |>
    mutate(converged = fit_ok(fit), bands = gc_bands[[ds]])
}, .id = "dataset")
save_tab(gear_contrast, "bag_gear_contrast")
gear_contrast |> select(dataset, term, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p) |> kable_round(3)
```

## Step 8: leave-one-vessel-out

The headline stage × season BAG refitted without each of the top
`r qparams$lovo_top_k` vessels per dataset × gear (by Primary hours in the
modelled stages), and without BUCKEYE (368175660), which the pre-Phase 4
screen kept but flagged. Each vessel's hours are removed from the cells,
stages and seasons it used.

```{r}
# the refits 09a ran (D-101), read only: a missing one stops the report
lovo <- lovo_refits(read_only = TRUE)
```

```{r}
lovo <- lovo |> mutate(MMSI = str_remove(tag, "^lovo_")) |> select(-any_of(c("vessel", "hours"))) |>
  left_join(distinct(lovo_vessels, MMSI, vessel), by = "MMSI") |>
  left_join(headline_rows(bag_rr) |> select(id, full_estimate = estimate), by = "id") |>
  mutate(rr = exp(estimate), shift = estimate - full_estimate)
save_tab(lovo, "bag_lovo")
lovo |> group_by(id) |>
  summarise(full_rr = exp(first(full_estimate)), min_rr = min(rr, na.rm = TRUE), max_rr = max(rr, na.rm = TRUE),
            most_influential = vessel[which.max(abs(shift))], .groups = "drop") |>
  kable_round(3)
lovo |> filter(MMSI == "368175660") |> select(id, vessel, rr, shift) |> kable_round(3)
```

## Step 8: fleet-size sensitivity

Caveat 5: part of the rise in AIS-tracked effort is AIS uptake, not more
fishing. The BAG contrast removes an AOI-wide uptake trend only if uptake is
spatially uniform across the bands. This refit adds the AOI-wide fleet size
per gear and time step, `log(n_mmsi_fleet + 1)` from the **VP** tables, as a
covariate. The VP count is used for AFE too, because the AFE count is partly
the outcome. Two refits per dataset × gear:

- **stage × season.** The fleet count has only 6 values (3 stages × 2
  seasons), and stage and season already use 4 degrees of freedom. Its
  coefficient is therefore weakly identified. It has no band variation, so
  the BAG terms should barely move. This refit confirms that.
- **timing.** The fleet count varies by month (by season-year for fixed AFE),
  so it competes with the year and month-of-year smooths for the AOI-wide
  trend. This is the more informative of the two.

A BAG rate ratio that moves by more than 10% is flagged. This is the same
threshold the plan uses for the environmental covariates (Phase 4 success
criteria). The fleet count can itself respond to the projects (vessels
leaving the AOI lower it), so this is a sensitivity, not a correction.

```{r}
# BAG rate ratios with and without the fleet term, for both model types.
# `terms`: the BAG terms of that model type. The timing models drop terms that
# do not exist for a gear (the post-construction terms), as in step 6.
fleet_pairs <- bind_rows(
  # each stage × season model's own BAG terms (D-076)
  ss_sets |> transmute(id, dataset, gear, model = "stage × season", base = spec, fleet = spec_fleet,
                       terms = terms),
  # only the timing models the support rule kept
  timing_sets |> filter(!map_lgl(spec_timing, is.null)) |>
    transmute(id, dataset, gear, model = "timing", base = spec_timing,
              fleet = spec_timing_fleet, terms = list(timing_terms)))

fleet_res <- fleet_pairs |>
  mutate(res = pmap(list(base, fleet, terms), function(s0, s1, terms) {
    t0 <- tidy(get_fit(s0))
    f1 <- get_fit(s1)
    t1 <- tidy(f1)
    terms <- intersect(terms, t0$term)
    # the fleet coefficient (log scale) is the elasticity of hours to fleet size
    lf <- t1 |> filter(term == "log_fleet")
    left_join(rate_ratios(t0, terms) |> select(term, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi),
              rate_ratios(t1, terms) |> select(term, rr_fleet = rr, rr_fleet_lo = rr_lo, rr_fleet_hi = rr_hi),
              by = "term") |>
      mutate(elasticity = lf$estimate, elasticity_se = lf$std.error, converged_fleet = fit_ok(f1))
  })) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, model, res) |> unnest(res) |>
  # % change in each BAG rate ratio when the fleet term is added; flagged above 10%
  mutate(pct_change = 100 * (rr_fleet / rr - 1), flag = abs(pct_change) > 10)
save_tab(fleet_res, "bag_fleet_sensitivity")

# the fleet elasticity per model, with a 95% Wald interval
fleet_res |> distinct(id, model, elasticity, elasticity_se, converged_fleet) |>
  mutate(lo = elasticity - 1.96 * elasticity_se, hi = elasticity + 1.96 * elasticity_se) |>
  select(id, model, elasticity, lo, hi, converged_fleet) |> kable_round(3)
fleet_res |> select(id, model, term, rr, rr_fleet, pct_change, flag) |> kable_round(3)

# headline-style terms side by side: points without and with the fleet term
p <- fleet_res |>
  filter(term %in% c(all_bag_terms, "cx_inside", "cx_0_2", "cx_near")) |>
  pivot_longer(c(rr, rr_fleet), names_to = "fit", values_to = "est") |>
  mutate(lo = if_else(fit == "rr", rr_lo, rr_fleet_lo), hi = if_else(fit == "rr", rr_hi, rr_fleet_hi),
         fit = factor(fit, c("rr", "rr_fleet"), c("without fleet", "with fleet"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(est, term, colour = fit)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.25) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("without fleet" = "grey55", "with fleet" = "#2a78d6")) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_grid(id ~ model, scales = "free") +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0)) +
  labs(x = "rate ratio (log scale)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "BAG rate ratios without and with the AOI-wide fleet-size covariate")
save_fig(p, "bag_fleet_sensitivity", height = 10)
p
```

## Summary and gate

```{r}
# `bands` says which headline each row is: inside × Stage 3 (full) or the
# pooled near band × Stage 3 (merged, D-076)
summary_tab <- headline_rows(bag_rr) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, bands, term, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, p, mde, descriptive_only) |>
  left_join(select(pretrend_gate, id, pretrend = verdict), by = "id") |>
  left_join(headline_rows(bag_rr_nozone) |> select(id, rr_no_zone = rr), by = "id") |>
  # the headline rate ratio with the fleet-size covariate (step 8)
  left_join(headline_rows(filter(fleet_res, model == "stage × season")) |>
              select(id, rr_fleet), by = "id")
save_tab(summary_tab, "bag_summary")
summary_tab |> kable_round(3)
```

Gate (plan, Phase 4):

- A dataset × gear with **MDE above 50%** (or none reached) is reported
  descriptively, with its MDE, not as a hypothesis test (`descriptive_only`).
- A **non-parallel** pre-trend verdict adds the `band × year` pre-trend term
  to that gear's BAG models; **inconclusive** makes the with- and without-term
  models co-primary. The pre-trend term is a Phase 7 sensitivity for every
  gear regardless (decision 2026-10-19, D-018).
- These are interim fits (decision 2026-10-20, D-047): Phase 5 confirms or replaces
  the spatial structure and families, and the power analysis and Phase 3's
  criterion 5 are then re-run on its base model.

### Reading the results (D-078)

This report holds dozens of estimates. They answer four questions, in this
order, and each question counts only if the one before it passed (plan,
@sec-bag-reading):

1. **Can the headline be read? (the gates)** Fitted under the support rule,
   converged, MDE at most 50%, pre-trend parallel, random-field check
   (D-077). DHARMa residuals are read by eye from Step 5's table: with tens
   of thousands of rows the tests reject for trivial misfit, so they are not
   automated here.
2. **What is the headline?** Stage 3 × inside (or near, if pooled) per
   dataset × gear, with its CI, read against the gear's MDE.
3. **Does it survive?** Each robustness check re-estimates the headline
   term and gets one outcome (`check_outcome()`): **shifted** if its
   estimate moves by more than the MDE or its verdict changes in substance
   (opposite direction, or between a detected change and "no change ≥
   MDE"); **weaker** or **stronger** if the verdict differs only because the
   CI is wider or narrower; otherwise **same**. Only a shifted check makes a
   headline "not robust": a narrower sample losing significance with the
   same estimate is lost precision, not a different answer. The counted
   checks are a short fixed list (below), because the more checks are
   counted, the more often one flips by chance.
4. **Why and when?** The Stage 2 terms (anticipation), the timing and leads
   models, foundation distance, the delta-Gamma parts and the gear contrast
   explain a headline; they never replace one.

**Beside the verdict, the gradient test** (D-091): the Wald test of all
Stage 3 × band terms of the headline fit, from Step 5's "Full stage × band
grid and gradient test". It says whether the gradient changed shape
anywhere, *gradient change detected* or *no evidence of a gradient change*,
and never alters the verdict. It cannot rule a change out: only the
verdict's *no change larger than the MDE* does that.

The rules are applied mechanically by `bag_gate()`, `bag_verdict()`,
`check_outcome()` and `bag_final_verdict()` (`r/bag_helpers.R`), so they
were fixed before any estimate was seen. Each gear ends in one verdict:
**change detected** (95% CI excludes 1), **no change larger than the MDE**
(90% CI inside ±MDE, the pre-trend test's equivalence reading),
**inconclusive** (neither), or **not interpretable** (a gate failed), each
marked robust or not. Across this many estimates about 1 in 20 will exclude
1 by chance, so a single surprising sensitivity row or lead bin is weak
evidence; agreement across checks, bands and the two datasets is what
counts.

**Counted checks** (`counted_checks` below): without safety-zone cells,
fleet-size covariate, leave one vessel out (here), and the fixed cohort
(Phase 7, D-074). Three Phase 7 runs have other roles and are not counted:

- **Exclusion upper bound** (D-074): its own column. Restoring the
  guard-vessel hours, which sit inside and along the lease edges, biases
  the estimate away from a decrease by construction. A shifted bound marks
  the verdict **classification-sensitive**: a finding about the safety
  vessels, not noise.
- **Pre-trend-term models**: their role follows the pre-trend gate. They
  **replace** the headline when the pre-trend is non-parallel (this is what
  "hold" waits for), are **co-primary** when it is inconclusive (a firm
  verdict needs both to agree), and are a reported sensitivity when it is
  parallel. They are fitted in the monthly timing model, because the stage
  × season model cannot hold a band × year trend alongside its Stage 2 and
  Stage 3 × band terms (three stage points per band), so they are compared
  with the timing model's construction × band term without the trend, not
  with this headline.
- **The rest of the Phase 7 sensitivity table** (2020 excluded, four
  seasons, covariates, exposure radii, …) is read together for patterns,
  not counted one by one.

Phase 7 calls the same helpers, appends its rows to `bag_reading_checks`
and writes the final `bag_reading`; this table is the interim one.

```{r}
# the random-field check's reading per model, if it ran (D-077): another
# structure meets the rule when it scores higher in total, in all but one
# fold, and has no failed fold
field_other <- if (exists("cv_scores")) {
  cv_scores |> filter(structure != "iid per stage") |> group_by(id) |>
    summarise(field_other = any(d_loglik > 0 & folds_better >= qparams$cv_folds - 1 & folds_ok == folds),
              .groups = "drop")
} else tibble(id = character(), field_other = logical())

# questions 1 and 2: the gate and the headline verdict per model
reading_head <- headline_rows(bag_rr) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, bands, term, estimate, std.error, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, mde, descriptive_only) |>
  left_join(transmute(ss_fits, id, converged = map_lgl(fit, fit_ok)), by = "id") |>
  left_join(select(pretrend_gate, id, pretrend = verdict), by = "id") |>
  left_join(field_other, by = "id") |>
  mutate(bag_gate(converged, descriptive_only, pretrend, field_other),
         verdict = bag_verdict(estimate, std.error, mde))

# question 4, the first piece: anticipation, from the Stage 2 term in the
# headline's band, with the same verdict rule
reading_s2 <- bag_rr |>
  semi_join(transmute(reading_head, id, term = str_replace(term, "Stage 3", "Stage 2")), by = c("id", "term")) |>
  left_join(select(reading_head, id, mde_h = mde), by = "id") |>
  transmute(id, stage2 = bag_verdict(estimate, std.error, mde_h), stage2_rr = rr)

# the checks that can make a headline "not robust", fixed before the
# freeze (D-078); "fixed cohort" arrives with Phase 7's rows
counted_checks <- c("without safety-zone cells", "fleet-size covariate", "leave one vessel out", "fixed cohort")

# question 3: every robustness estimate of the headline term, on the log
# scale with its standard error (the fleet table keeps the CI, so its SE is
# recovered from it)
se_of_ci <- \(lo, hi) (log(hi) - log(lo)) / (2 * qnorm(0.975))
robust_rows <- bind_rows(
  headline_rows(bag_rr_nozone) |>
    transmute(id, check = "without safety-zone cells", label = check, estimate, se = std.error),
  # a fleet refit that did not converge is shown as failed, not dropped
  headline_rows(filter(fleet_res, model == "stage × season")) |>
    transmute(id, check = "fleet-size covariate", label = check,
              estimate = if_else(converged_fleet, log(rr_fleet), NA_real_),
              se = if_else(converged_fleet, se_of_ci(rr_fleet_lo, rr_fleet_hi), NA_real_)),
  # one row per vessel left out; failed refits are NA
  lovo |> transmute(id, check = "leave one vessel out", label = paste("without", coalesce(vessel, MMSI)),
                    estimate, se = std.error)) |>
  left_join(select(reading_head, id, est_head = estimate, verdict_head = verdict, mde), by = "id") |>
  mutate(outcome = check_outcome(estimate, se, est_head, verdict_head, mde),
         counted = check %in% counted_checks)
save_tab(robust_rows, "bag_reading_checks")

# per model: how many counted checks ran, how many shifted the conclusion or
# only weakened it, and which rows did (a check with several rows, like LOVO,
# shifts it if any row does, and the vessel is named)
robust_by_id <- robust_rows |>
  filter(counted) |>
  group_by(id, check) |>
  summarise(failed = sum(is.na(outcome)), shifted = any(outcome %in% "shifted"),
            weaker = any(outcome %in% "weaker"),
            by = paste(label[outcome %in% "shifted"], collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(checks = n(), checks_shifted = sum(shifted), checks_weaker = sum(weaker),
            refits_failed = sum(failed), shifted_by = paste(by[nzchar(by)], collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")

# the verdict table: one line per dataset × gear. `bound` (the exclusion
# upper bound's outcome) stays NA until Phase 7 adds it
# the gradient test of the headline fit (D-091), beside the verdict and not
# part of it, so bag_final_verdict() does not see it. With it, the test's
# false-positive rate (e = 0) and its power against the fading gradient
# (Step 3): "no evidence of a gradient change" from a test with low fading
# power says little about displacement
reading_grad <- gradient_test |> filter(headline_fit) |> select(id, gradient_p = p, gradient) |>
  left_join(gradient_power |> filter(effect == 0) |> transmute(id, gradient_fpr = power), by = "id") |>
  left_join(gradient_power |> filter(scenario == "fading") |> transmute(id, gradient_power_fading = power),
            by = "id")
reading <- reading_head |>
  left_join(reading_s2, by = "id") |>
  left_join(robust_by_id, by = "id") |>
  left_join(reading_grad, by = "id") |>
  mutate(checks_shifted = coalesce(checks_shifted, 0L), bound = NA_character_,
         final = bag_final_verdict(gate, verdict, checks_shifted, mde, bound)) |>
  select(id, dataset, gear, bands, gate, gate_reasons, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, mde, verdict,
         stage2, stage2_rr, checks, checks_shifted, checks_weaker, refits_failed, shifted_by, bound, final,
         gradient_p, gradient, gradient_fpr, gradient_power_fading)
save_tab(reading, "bag_reading")
reading |> select(id, bands, gate, rr, rr_lo, rr_hi, mde, verdict, stage2, checks, checks_shifted, checks_weaker, final,
                  gradient, gradient_power_fading) |>
  kable_round(2)
# the reasons and the rows that shifted a conclusion, where there are any
reading |> filter(nzchar(gate_reasons) | nzchar(coalesce(shifted_by, ""))) |>
  select(id, gate_reasons, shifted_by) |> knitr::kable()
```

One panel per dataset × gear: the headline (dark), each robustness variant
(blue) and every leave-one-vessel-out refit (grey points), with 95% CIs.
The shaded band is ±MDE around no change: an estimate inside it is smaller
than the gear could reliably detect.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
forest_rows <- c("headline", "without safety-zone cells", "fleet-size covariate", "leave one vessel out")
forest <- bind_rows(
  reading_head |> transmute(id, row = "headline", estimate, se = std.error),
  robust_rows |> transmute(id, row = check, estimate, se)) |>
  filter(!is.na(estimate)) |>
  mutate(rr = exp(estimate), lo = exp(estimate - qnorm(0.975) * se), hi = exp(estimate + qnorm(0.975) * se),
         kind = case_when(row == "headline" ~ "headline", row == "leave one vessel out" ~ "lovo", TRUE ~ "variant"),
         row = factor(row, rev(forest_rows))) |>
  # the panel title carries the band scheme, since a pooled headline is a
  # different quantity (D-076), and the gear's verdict
  left_join(transmute(reading, id, panel = paste0(id, " (", bands, "): ", final)), by = "id")
mde_band <- reading |> filter(!is.na(mde)) |>
  transmute(panel = paste0(id, " (", bands, "): ", final), lo = 1 - mde, hi = 1 / (1 - mde))
p <- ggplot(forest, aes(rr, row)) +
  geom_rect(data = mde_band, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(data = filter(forest, kind == "lovo"), colour = "grey45", alpha = 0.6, size = 1,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.15, seed = 1)) +
  geom_pointrange(data = filter(forest, kind != "lovo"), aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, colour = kind), size = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(headline = "#0d366b", variant = "#2a78d6"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x", labeller = label_wrap_gen(80)) +
  labs(x = "headline rate ratio, Stage 3 × inside or near band (log scale)", y = NULL,
       title = "Headline BAG estimate and its robustness checks",
       subtitle = "shaded: ±MDE around no change; grey points: one vessel left out")
save_fig(p, "bag_reading", height = 9)
p
```
